facts.detail: The updated broadband speed codes apply to purchases from 21 December 2022.
The speed codes are voluntary protections supplied by participating providers rather than a universal coverage dataset.

guard_streams.write_limit: Code participation cannot establish postcode availability.

facts.detail: The current official page lists BT, EE, NOW Broadband, Plusnet, Sky, TalkTalk, Utility Warehouse, Virgin Media and Zen for residential protections.
The current official page lists BT, TalkTalk and Virgin Media for the business code.

guard_streams.write_limit: A provider-signatory list is not evidence that a specific property is served.

facts.detail: Participating providers give an expected speed range in writing when a contract starts.
Customers receive a minimum guaranteed speed before agreeing to a new deal.

guard_streams.write_limit: Contractual estimates and guarantees are not measured parcel speeds.

facts.detail: The strengthened code requires information on speeds expected during busy peak periods.
Personalised estimates can use the capability of the line entering the individual home or office rather than only a similar-property group.

guard_streams.write_limit: A sales estimate cannot replace the exact official coverage archive.

facts.detail: Where the provider-network problem leaves service below the promised speed, the provider has 30 days to resolve it.
If unresolved, customers may leave without an early-exit fee and the protection extends to associated bundled services.

guard_streams.write_limit: A contractual remedy does not prove historical or current postcode coverage.

facts.detail: The business code applies regardless of business size for participating providers.
Its standard-service scope spans ADSL, cable, FTTC, FTTP, wireless and satellite, while dedicated or guaranteed-speed services are excluded.

guard_streams.write_limit: Business-code coverage is not equivalent to Ofcom all-premises fixed coverage.

facts.detail: Ofcom advises multiple speed tests over several days and at different times.
A speed test indicates the connection experience at the test time, not universal postcode availability.

guard_streams.write_limit: Consumer test results must not be assigned to untested parcels.

facts.detail: Distance from the exchange, time of day and simultaneous household use can reduce experienced speed.
Device configuration, line damage and provider traffic-management policies can also affect performance.

guard_streams.write_limit: Temporary or local performance factors do not alter the official archive row without source evidence.

facts.detail: In-home Wi-Fi cannot exceed the underlying broadband service performance.
The wireless router-to-device link can itself become a performance bottleneck.

guard_streams.write_limit: Wi-Fi performance must not be recorded as fixed access-line availability.

facts.detail: A direct Ethernet connection often provides a faster and more reliable test path than Wi-Fi.
The Ethernet cable must support the broadband speed or it can limit measured performance.

guard_streams.write_limit: A wired test is a diagnostic control, not a postcode-level source.

facts.detail: Router placement, intervening objects and placing equipment on the floor can weaken Wi-Fi.
Electrical devices and nearby wireless equipment can interfere with router signals.

guard_streams.write_limit: In-home interference cannot be interpreted as absence of external network coverage.

facts.detail: Mesh systems can improve in-home signal coverage but do not increase the underlying broadband service rate.
Repeaters can reduce responsiveness or speed, while powerline performance depends on the electrical wiring.

guard_streams.write_limit: Home-network improvements cannot produce an official parcel speed candidate.
